use: scripts/test_jobs.py submit --matrix docs/test-footage/clip-mix-v1.json -k 2 --state run.json (docs/runbooks/test-jobs.md). Rows with footage_uploaded false, or no footage_id, are skipped; a row the website finds no clip for is named and skipped. Rows run in order: the paths most likely to break and the cheapest first.
adding_a_clip: For a row that needs the owner: download the clip from its source_page, make walkthrough.mp4 with the row's prepare command (the bucket takes only walkthrough.mp4 or .mov; Commons serves WebM and Ogg), write source.json beside it (source_page, licence_text: the row's licence_line, sha256 of walkthrough.mp4, added_by, added_at), upload both to internal-test-footage/<footage_id>/, then set footage_uploaded to true. A clip is added only on the owner's word (docs/runbooks/test-jobs.md).
money: About $10-15 a job, under the $40 cap. The runner stops before a row when the month's counted spend plus $20 reaches the $400 November limit: with about $310 counted, that is about four more jobs this month; the limit is $300 again from December.
licences: Licence lines are copied from each Commons file page's Licensing section, read on 2026-11-24. The Pexels rows' pages could not be read from this network (HTTP 403) and are marked licence not checked; the readiness plan already asks counsel about the Pexels stock clips (docs/launch-readiness/2026-11-beta-readiness-plan.md, O-07).
descriptions: Each description is one sentence as a site would write it, drafted from the source page's own description; none of these clips was watched here.

atlas_source_geometry: the exact source-to-geometry pixel transform, including the display rotation (docs/website-atlas-scene-source.md)
